MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles.summary: Neither library has algebraic cycles modulo an adequate equivalence, correspondences, or any category of motives: 'Chow', 'motive', 'Tannakian category', 'numerical equivalence' and 'Weil cohomology' return no mathematical declaration in either tree. What is genuinely present and reusable is categorical rather than motivic: Mathlib's Karoubi envelope with its universal property (`CategoryTheory.Idempotents.karoubiUniversal`, `functorExtension`), rigid monoidal categories with duals, pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes, and an unquotiented cycle group with proper pushforward (`AlgebraicGeometry.AlgebraicCycle.map`, functoriality unproved); Tau Ceti supplies pure and mixed Hodge structures with Tate twists, polarizations and semisimplicity, and a sorry-free Tannakian reconstruction of an affine group scheme from its category of finite-dimensional comodules (`TauCeti.Tannaka.tensorAutFunctor`). Everything specific to this roadmap — Chow groups, correspondence composition, pure and mixed motive categories, realizations and cycle classes, Jannsen semisimplicity, Nori's diagram category, motivic Galois groups and the cycle conjectures — is missing. The roadmap should also be reconciled with SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5 and MotivicEtaleKTheory M.4/M.5a, which promise the same cycle and correspondence groups.

targets.note: Neither library defines a Chow group or rational equivalence of cycles. targets.note: Mathlib defines pushforward `AlgebraicCycle.map` for a quasi-compact morphism, weighted by user-supplied dimension functions and the residue degree, and proves only `map_id`. targets.target: Idempotent completion (Karoubi envelope) of an additive/preadditive category
targets.note: `CategoryTheory.Idempotents.Karoubi C` is the pseudo-abelian completion of an arbitrary category, with `toKaroubi` the canonical embedding, preadditive and finite-biproduct structure (`Biproducts.lean`), and idempotent-completeness of the result. This is strictly more general than the pseudo-abelian envelope of a correspondence category. No `sorry` in the `Idempotents` directory.

targets.target: Universal extension of additive functors through idempotent completion
targets.note: `karoubiUniversal₁ C D : (C ⥤ Karoubi D) ≌ (Karoubi C ⥤ Karoubi D)` is the universal property in the form that assumes nothing of `D`, and `functorExtension₁` is the extension functor underlying it. The form MC.1 will use — `karoubiUniversal C D : (C ⥤ D) ≌ (Karoubi C ⥤ D)` and `functorExtension : (C ⥤ D) ⥤ (Karoubi C ⥤ D)`, with the intermediate `karoubiUniversal₂ : (C ⥤ D) ≌ (Karoubi C ⥤ Karoubi D)` — carries `[IsIdempotentComplete D]`, which is exactly what makes functors out of the idempotent completion land in `D` itself. All are proved for arbitrary categories, so a fortiori for preadditive correspondence categories.

AInfCohomology.summary: Mathlib supplies more of the AI.0 period-ring prefix than the roadmap document assumes: the tilt of any p-adically complete ring (`PreTilt`, perfect and of characteristic p), hence A_inf = W(O^♭) with `WittVector.frobeniusEquiv`; Fontaine's θ (`WittVector.fontaineTheta`) with surjectivity and the Teichmüller formula; the untilt map; and B_dR^+ and B_dR defined exactly as the ker-θ-adic completion of A_inf[1/p] and its localization. It also has ℂ_p and its ring of integers, F-isocrystals with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification, divided-power structures, continuous group cohomology, derived categories and abstract sheaf cohomology. Everything else this roadmap needs is missing from both libraries: μ, ξ and ξ̃ (ker θ principal is still an explicit Mathlib TODO), θ̃, the residue map to W(k), Breuil–Kisin twists, PD envelopes and A_cris, the décalage operator Lη and derived completeness, BKF modules and Fargues' equivalence, adic spaces and their pro-étale sites, AΩ, de Rham–Witt, crystalline and étale cohomology, log structures, Hyodo–Kato and prismatic cohomology. AI.1–AI.7 are therefore not built; AI.0 and its integral substage are partly built, and the layers overlap heavily with PadicHodgeTheory R06.1, CrystallineCohomology CR.0/CR.4/CR.5/CR.6, PrismaticCohomology PR.0/PR.6/PR.7 and CohomologyComparisons CP.1/CP.4/CP.5.

AdicEtaleGeometry.summary: Tau Ceti already owns the predecessor layer this roadmap starts from, and owns it in depth: Huber rings and pairs with pairs of definition, pseudouniformizers and completion; restricted power series A⟨T⟩ and topologically-finite-type maps; rational subsets with their basis, perturbation invariance and refinement calculus; rational localisation A⟨T/s⟩ with its universal property, flatness and faithful flatness over a finite rational cover; Spa(A,A⁺) with its functorial comap; a presentation-indexed structure presheaf and a criterion reducing sheafhood to rational covers; the closed polydisc; and the full analytic-locus theory, including Tate charts on the analytic locus of a non-Tate pair — all sorry-free. What is missing is everything that makes this roadmap a successor rather than a predecessor: there is no adic space object, no structure sheaf identified with 𝒪_X, no completed tensor product or fibre product, no uniform or perfectoid rings, no étale or finite étale morphisms of adic spaces, no étale or pro-étale site, no differentials/Jacobian criterion/smoothness in the analytic setting, no analytification, no formal schemes, and no pseudocoherent module theory. A0, A1 and A2 are partly built (the analytic locus and Tate charts, the finite-module topology over a Tate ring, and the closed polydisc are genuinely present); A3 and A4 are not built. The roadmap also overlaps AdicSpacesPartII R0–R4 and F0 by design — A0 and A2 name it as canonical owner — so the two documents must not both construct the fibre products.

targets.target: Topology on the tensor product of compatible complete Huber pairs, its separated completion, and the plus subring as the integral closure of the image
targets.note: There is no completed tensor product anywhere in either library: `grep -rn -i 'tensor' TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace` only finds flatness arguments. Tau Ceti does have Huber pairs, rings of integral elements, completion of a Huber ring (with its pair of definition) and the fact that Spa is unchanged by replacing A⁺ by its integral closure, i.e. the pieces the construction would use.

targets.target: Universal property of the completed tensor product for continuous morphisms of Huber pairs
targets.note: Absent. The only universal property of this shape in Tau Ceti is `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_locTopology` for the rational localisation A⟨T/s⟩ (Wedhorn 5.51).

targets.target: Uniformization of a Huber pair and its universal property
targets.note: Neither library defines a uniform Huber/Tate ring (`grep -rn -i 'IsUniform\|uniform ring\|uniform Tate'` over the Huber tree is empty), so uniformization and its universal property are absent.

targets.target: Existence of pullbacks along rational open immersions
targets.note: The affine half is present: A⟨T/s⟩ with its topology and universal property, and `spaLocalizationHomeomorph` identifying Spa of the (uncompleted) rational localisation with R(T/s). Missing is any category of adic spaces in which to form a pullback — Tau Ceti has no `AdicSpace` object and the structure presheaf is not yet identified with 𝒪_X.

targets.target: Pullbacks along finite étale maps, and the extension to locally finite-type/noetherian cases
targets.note: No finite étale morphism of Huber pairs or adic spaces exists (`grep -rn -i 'etale' TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace` is empty). Mathlib's étale and finite morphisms are for schemes only.

targets.target: Gluing the affine constructions, the categorical pullback property, chart independence, associativity and unit comparison maps with coherence
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti has a presentation-indexed presheaf on Spa and a criterion reducing sheafhood to rational covers, but neither the structure sheaf nor an adic-space category, so there is nothing to glue.

targets.target: The analytic locus of Spa(A,A⁺), and Tate charts on it for a non-Tate Huber pair
targets.note: Fully constructed and sorry-free in Tau Ceti: `spaAnalytic` (Wedhorn 7.39), its openness and quasi-compactness, equality with the whole spectrum for a Tate ring, the finite rational cover by the generators of an ideal of definition, and — exactly A0's 'Tate charts on their analytic loci' — that the completed rational localisation at such a generator is a Tate ring. This works for non-Tate Huber pairs such as Witt rings, as A0 requires.

targets.target: Morphism restriction interfaces for analytic adic spaces over Spa(ℤ_p,ℤ_p)
targets.note: `spaComap` with continuity, contravariant functoriality and compatibility with rational subsets is the affine restriction interface; but there are no analytic adic spaces and no base Spa(ℤ_p,ℤ_p) object, so the morphism-restriction interface A0 specifies cannot be stated.

targets.target: Tracking changes of rings of definition, pseudouniformizers and plus rings
targets.note: Tau Ceti carries a pair of definition as explicit data with a refinement order and presentations, has `IsPseudoUniformizer`, transports pairs of definition through completion, and proves `spa_antitone`/`spa_integralClosure` for changes of plus ring. This bookkeeping is the one A0 names and it is in place.

duplicates.note: A0 itself names AdicSpacesPartII as the canonical owner; R0 states the same completed tensor product, plus-ring construction, universal property and gluing to fibre products.
F0 says it 'includes original diamond AdicEtaleGeometry A0 and ordinary geometric portions of A1–A2', so the fibre-product constructions are duplicated verbatim.
P2 owns rational localization and sheafiness for perfectoid Huber pairs and the perfectoid pullback theorem A0 defers to it.
Tau Ceti's own AdicSpaces Layer 0–3 already owns Huber pairs, pairs of definition, pseudouniformizers, rational localisation and its universal property — the supplier A0 assumes.

targets.target: The canonical topology on a finite (étale) algebra over a complete Tate Huber pair, with continuity and uniqueness
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Wedhorn Proposition 6.18(1) in full: for a complete Hausdorff (noetherian) Tate ring and a finite module, the module topology is first countable, nonarchimedean, complete and Hausdorff, and is the unique such topology. That is more general than the finite-étale case A1 asks for.

targets.target: The integral plus ring of a finite étale algebra and its affinoid spectrum, with compatibility with rational restriction
targets.note: Rings of integral elements, Spa of an arbitrary pair, and compatibility of `spaComap` with rational subsets exist, but the plus ring of a finite étale algebra is not constructed and there is no sheafiness statement for it.

targets.note: Absent from both libraries; Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Etale` and `IsOpenImmersion` are properties of morphisms of schemes.

targets.note: Tau Ceti's `Spv`/`spa` are rank-agnostic (a point is a valuative relation with no chosen value group) and the analytic-point theory explicitly handles height-one generizations of higher-rank points, so the objects exist; what is missing is their use as points of a site, since no site exists.

targets.target: Pro-étale covers in Scholze's corrected form (arbitrary transfinite towers whose successor maps are pullbacks of finite étale surjections)
targets.note: Mathlib's pro-étale site is for schemes and is defined through weakly étale morphisms, not through transfinite towers; nothing corresponding exists for adic spaces.

targets.target: Generalized adic-space presentations and their agreement with sheafy adic spaces
targets.note: Absent. Tau Ceti has a presentation-indexed limit presheaf, explicitly documented as not yet identified with 𝒪_X, and no notion of sheafy Huber pair or adic space.

duplicates.note: R4 is declared to be the 'early site reexport' of A1 — 'transport the elementary site and sheaf operations from A1 without constructing a second site'.
A1's own first paragraph assigns the ordinary finite/étale morphism constructions to AdicSpacesPartII's early prefix, which is R0.
D2 'Pro-étale and v-topologies' constructs the pro-étale topology on the diamond side; the corrected covering convention must be stated once.

targets.target: Diagonals, separated, proper and partially proper morphisms of analytic adic spaces, with valuative criteria and comparison to Huber's definitions
targets.note: Mathlib has `IsSeparated`, `IsProper` and the `ValuativeCriterion` for morphisms of schemes, sorry-free; there is no adic-space analogue in either library, and no adic-space category to carry a diagonal.

targets.target: Finite-dimensional analytic balls (closed polydiscs)
targets.note: Tau Ceti constructs the closed polydisc Spa(A⟨T₁,…,T_k⟩, A⟨T⟩°) over a nonarchimedean ring, with its classical points given by evaluation at power-bounded tuples and their injectivity at trivial-support points (Wedhorn Example 7.57). Sorry-free.

targets.note: Laurent rational subsets and the associated Laurent series rings are built (`Huber/LaurentSeries.lean`, `LocalizationTopology/Laurent/*`), but there is no analytic torus object: `grep -rn -i 'torus\|annulus'` over the Huber and AdicSpace trees is empty.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has Wedhorn §6.6 at the ring level — `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, its strict variant, and their interaction with strong noetherianity — but not the morphism-of-spaces notion, since adic spaces are not constructed.

targets.target: Continuous Kähler differentials in the finite-presentation setting and the analytic Jacobian criterion
targets.note: Mathlib's `KaehlerDifferential` is the purely algebraic module of differentials; there is no completed/continuous variant and no Jacobian criterion in the analytic setting in either library.

targets.target: Smooth morphisms; smooth is locally étale over a relative ball; base change, composition and dimension estimates
targets.note: Absent for adic spaces; Mathlib's `Smooth` is a scheme morphism property.

targets.target: Adic analytification of finite-type schemes over a nonarchimedean field and the relative version over an affinoid pair
targets.note: Absent: `grep -rn -i 'analytification\|rigid analytic'` over both Lean trees finds only bibliography lines.

targets.target: Formal schemes, admissible formal models and their generic fibres
targets.note: Absent: there is no `Spf`, no formal scheme and no admissible blow-up in either library.

duplicates.note: A2 names AdicSpacesPartII as canonical owner; R0 states the separatedness, finite, smooth and étale morphism package.
R1 owns the adic analytification of finite-type schemes and the properness/GAGA comparison A2 also lists.

targets.note: `pseudocoherent` occurs nowhere in either library. Tau Ceti has the flatness chain that the gluing argument rests on — flatness of rational restriction maps and faithful flatness/injectivity of A → ∏ A⟨Tᵢ/sᵢ⟩ over a finite rational cover — plus a criterion reducing sheafhood to rational covers, but not Tate acyclicity itself and no module-level exactness theory.

targets.note: The relative ball exists (`closedPolydisc`), but there are no closed embeddings of adic spaces, no ideal sheaves and no conormal sequence in the analytic setting.

targets.target: That ideal sheaf is the sheaf of a pseudocoherent module, with the affine quotient and plus-ring description

targets.note: Tau Ceti proves a quantitative perturbation theorem (Wedhorn 7.34, strengthened to an arbitrary Huber ring): sufficiently small perturbations of the numerators and denominator leave the rational subset unchanged. That is a perturbation statement about rational subsets, not about the equations of an étale space, and no implicit-function theorem in this setting exists.

targets.note: Absent; requires the perfectoid tower and the whole preceding chain.

targets.note: There is no étale category for adic spaces in either library.

targets.target: The cofiltered system of finite étale torsors with no remaining nonsplit finite étale covers
targets.note: Absent; finite étale covers of adic spaces do not exist.

targets.target: Perfectoidness of the uniform completion, with the pseudouniformizer and Frobenius-surjectivity arguments
targets.note: No perfectoid ring or space is defined in either library; Mathlib's perfectoid directory contains only the tilt-based period rings and states no perfectoid condition. Tau Ceti has pseudouniformizers but nothing about Frobenius surjectivity on A/p.

targets.target: Invariance and effectivity of the finite étale data along the tower, and the compactness condition for surjectivity of a v-sheaf
targets.note: Absent; v-sheaves do not exist in either library.

targets.target: The local analytic presentation of §15: a perfectoid cover with its perfectoid equivalence relation, or a generalized-affinoid presentation
targets.note: Absent; depends on all the previous targets.

AdicSpacesPartII.summary: The libraries have essentially nothing of this roadmap's successor material. There is no formal scheme, no Spf, no formal GAGA, no analytification, no dagger or overconvergent algebra, no completed tensor product of Huber pairs, no fibre product of adic spaces, no coherent sheaf theory on an affinoid, no Kiehl finiteness, no analytic trace and no étale or pro-étale site of an adic space; Tau Ceti has no `AdicSpace` object at all and its structure presheaf on Spa is explicitly not yet identified with 𝒪_X. What is genuinely in place and reusable is the affine prefix: Huber pairs with completion, restricted power series and topologically-finite-type maps, strong noetherianity, rational localisation A⟨T/s⟩ with its universal property, flatness of restriction maps and faithful flatness over a finite rational cover, a sheafhood criterion on rational covers, the closed embedding induced by a quotient Huber pair, the base change M ⊗_A A⟨T⟩ ≅ M⟨T⟩, the closed polydisc, and — on the algebraic side — Mathlib's `Algebra.trace` with transitivity and localization compatibility, its quasi-coherent affine equivalence, and its étale/pro-étale sites for schemes. F0, F1 and R0–R3 and R5 are not built; R4 is a declared reexport of AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and is process. The roadmap overlaps AdicEtaleGeometry A0–A3 by design and further overlaps PerfectoidSpaces P2/P9 and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0 for the dagger algebras.

targets.target: Spf(A) for a complete separated noetherian adic ring, with its structure sheaf, independence of the ideal of definition and gluing
targets.note: There is no formal scheme in either library: `grep -rn -i 'formal scheme\|\bSpf\b'` over both Lean trees returns only a bibliography line. Mathlib has `AdicCompletion` of rings and modules with functoriality, which is the affine algebra only.

targets.target: Equivalence of Spf with compatible systems of schemes modulo powers of the ideal of definition
targets.note: Absent; no formal-scheme carrier.

targets.target: Functorial completion along a closed subscheme
targets.note: Only the ring/module-level adic completion and its functoriality exist; there is no completion of a scheme along a closed subscheme.

targets.target: Affine coherent-module equivalence, formal functions and formal GAGA in the proper finite-presentation setting with ample line bundle
targets.note: Mathlib proves the affine quasi-coherent equivalence for schemes (`tildeEquiv`, `isQuasicoherent_iff_isIso_fromTildeΓ`), but the theorem on formal functions and Grothendieck existence/algebraization are absent from both libraries (`grep -rn -i 'formal function\|Grothendieck existence'` finds nothing).

targets.target: Locally strongly noetherian analytic fibre products from admissible completed tensor products
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the strongly-noetherian predicate and Mathlib has pullbacks of schemes with the affine formula `pullbackSpecIso`, but there is no completed tensor product of Huber pairs and no analytic-space category to form the fibre product in.

targets.target: Stability of finite and étale morphisms under these fibre products, and implicit-function/Jacobian local criteria
targets.note: Absent: no étale morphisms of adic spaces and no analytic implicit-function theorem in either library.

targets.target: Properness, separatedness and smoothness comparisons with formal models and finite-type analytification
targets.note: Mathlib has these properties for morphisms of schemes only; there is no analytification and no formal model to compare with.

H1 constructs formal schemes of Huber's type (S) and the specialization map, overlapping F0's formal-scheme prefix.
C3's proper coherent GAGA is the archimedean twin of F0's formal GAGA/algebraization statement.

targets.target: Weakly complete dagger affinoid algebras, radius-indexed presentations and comparison with completed rigid/adic affinoids
targets.note: `dagger`, `overconvergent` and `weakly complete` appear nowhere in either Lean tree. Tau Ceti's completed restricted power series A⟨T⟩ are the affinoid side of the comparison, with nothing overconvergent to compare them to.

targets.target: Independence of presentations and cofinal systems of strict neighbourhoods
targets.note: Absent; `strict neighborhood` has no occurrence in either library.

targets.target: Restriction, completed/overconvergent tensor products and admissible gluing for dagger spaces
targets.note: Absent; there is no completed tensor product of topological algebras at all.

targets.target: Coherent dagger modules, differential forms, exterior derivative and the logarithmic complex for a strict normal crossings boundary
targets.note: Mathlib has the algebraic module of Kähler differentials but no de Rham complex of a scheme or analytic space, and no logarithmic structures anywhere.

CohomologyComparisons.summary: This roadmap compares cohomology theories that neither library has: there is no crystalline, log-crystalline, Hyodo–Kato, de Rham, de Rham–Witt, prismatic or AΩ cohomology, no étale cohomology of an adic space, no formal schemes or adic generic fibres, no A_cris/B_cris/B_st, no Breuil–Kisin twists or modules, no Chern classes or dlog maps, and no monodromy operator. The only pieces already present are coefficient-level: Mathlib's Fontaine θ, the Witt Frobenius and functoriality, B_dR^+ and B_dR as rings (constructed exactly as CP.0 describes, but with no θ-extension, filtration or DVR property proved), the p-adic cyclotomic character, F-isocrystals with the one-dimensional Dieudonné–Manin classification, divided-power structures without an envelope, `Module.length` for the CP.5 torsion inequalities, continuous group cohomology, and Tau Ceti's Kummer map Kˣ → H¹(G_K,μ_n). All seven layers are not built. Because CP is by design an assembly roadmap, every layer restates targets owned elsewhere — AI.0/AI.4/AI.5/AI.6, CR.0/CR.2/CR.6, PR.4/PR.6/PR.8, R06.1–R06.6, R07.3–R07.4 and RT.5–RT.6 — so the boundary that matters is that CP proves compatibility rather than constructing any of these maps a second time.

targets.note: None of the four carriers exists: there is no formal scheme, no adic/rigid generic fibre, no pro-étale site of an adic space and no log site in either library.

targets.note: Absent. Mathlib supplies ℂ_p and its ring of integers as the base object but no cohomology of a formal model to compare.

targets.note: θ and the Witt Frobenius/functoriality exist in Mathlib and the p-adic cyclotomic character is defined with its Hodge–Tate normalization implicit in `cyclotomicCharacter`; ξ, ξ̃, μ, θ̃ and the Breuil–Kisin uniformizer do not exist, so most of the dictionary has no entries to normalize.

targets.target: All ring maps from the shared objects to A_cris, B_cris, B_st and B_dR
targets.note: Only the B_dR side exists: B_dR^+ is constructed in Mathlib directly as the ker-θ-adic completion of A_inf[1/p], with the structure map `AdicCompletion.of`. A_cris, B_cris and B_st are absent because Mathlib has divided power structures but no PD envelope.
